info:
Temporal Shift(تحوّل زمني):
In classical language, it denotes past existence ("he was") or shifts a present state to the past.

Timeless / Eternal Presence (الدَّوَام وَالِاسْتِمْرَار):
When كَانَ is used in reference to Allah and His attributes, it does not denote a past state. It signifies an absolute, permanent, and timeless truth—implying that a quality always was, currently is, and will forever be true.

Certainty of Future Events (تَحْقِيق الْوُقُوع):
Using كَانَ for a future promise or decree signals that the event is so guaranteed to happen that it can be spoken of as if it has already occurred.
examples: كَانُواْ لَا يَتَنَاهَوۡنَ عَن مُّنكَرٖ فَعَلُوهُۚ [5:79]
وَيُسۡقَوۡنَ فِيهَا كَأۡسٗا كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلًا [76:17]

info:
Linguistically:
carries the connotation of deliberate effort in taking, adopting, or fashioning something for oneself (due to the Form VIII structure, which often denotes self-reflexivity or intensity).

In the Quran:
When humans are the subject, the Quran uses ittakhadha to expose a deliberate, misplaced psychological substitution.

When Allah is the subject of ittakhadha, it denotes a profound, deliberate honoring of a creation, elevating them to an irreplaceable status.
examples: إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ فَاتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّا [35:6]
يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰ   لَيۡتَنِي   لَمۡ   أَتَّخِذۡ   فُلَانًا   خَلِيلٗا [25:28]

Causal Object: قُل لَّوۡ أَنتُمۡ تَمۡلِكُونَ خَزَآئِنَ رَحۡمَةِ رَبِّيٓ إِذٗا لَّأَمۡسَكۡتُمۡ خَشۡيَةَ ٱلۡإِنفَاقِۚ [17:100]
وَعَلَّمۡنَٰهُ صَنۡعَةَ لَبُوسٖ لَّكُمۡ لِتُحۡصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأۡسِكُمۡۖ [21:80]
Adverbial Object: وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ طَرَفَيِ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَزُلَفٗا مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِۚ [11:114]
Circumstantial: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡقَمَرَ بَازِغٗا قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ [6:77]
إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ [28:71]
